record.paper_title: String Theory on ADS3: Some Open Questions
record.original_question: Can a less formal treatment of string theory on AdS3—using the classical SU(1,1) Wess–Zumino–Witten model, classical string motion, a path-integral formulation, and explicit target-space boundary conditions—recover the physically expected states with j < k/2 that are cut off by the current-algebra analysis, clarify the role of continuous-series representations, and reveal whether boundary conditions create quantization ambiguities for strings analogous to those for particles on AdS3?

evidence.quote: we should get a better understanding of the SU(1,1) WZW model at the classical level, explore the classical motion of a string, and maybe try to follow a path-integral approach à la Gawȩdzki.
This implies in particular a proper treatment of the target-space boundary conditions that are hard to implement within the current-algebra method.
They might play a role in reconciling unitarity with the appearance of states of the discrete series with spin j < k/2, i.e. with mass above the anti-de Sitter radius scale.
The role of continuous series could also be clarified.
one should wonder whether target-space boundary conditions introduce ambiguities in the quantization of a string, similar to those appearing when solving the wave equation for a quantum particle.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider bosonic string theory on three-dimensional anti–de Sitter space AdS₃, formulated as a Wess–Zumino–Witten (WZW) sigma model with target the group manifold SU(1,1) ≃ SL(2,ℝ) (or its universal cover) at level k. The unitary irreducible representations of the affine sl(2,ℝ) current algebra include the principal continuous series and the highest/lowest-weight discrete series D±_j parameterized by a spin j > 0. A standard current-algebra (no-ghost) analysis imposes the unitarity restriction j < k/2 on physical states, but classical string motions on AdS₃ suggest the existence of physically sensible string states whose effective spin lies in the range cut off by this bound (corresponding to masses above the AdS curvature scale).

(a) Develop a treatment of the classical SU(1,1) WZW model — including the analysis of classical string trajectories on AdS₃ and a Gawędzki-style path-integral quantization — that recovers the physically expected string states with j ≥ k/2 (or otherwise reconciles unitarity with the appearance of such states above the AdS radius mass scale).

(b) In this framework, clarify the role played by the continuous-series representations of SL(2,ℝ) in the physical Hilbert space of the string.

(c) Implement explicit target-space boundary conditions at the conformal boundary of AdS₃ within the path-integral formulation, and determine whether the choice of such boundary conditions produces quantization ambiguities for the string analogous to the well-known boundary-condition ambiguities encountered when quantizing a relativistic point particle on AdS₃.
artifact.status_search_result: The questions raised about the SL(2,ℝ) WZW spectrum on AdS₃ were substantially resolved by Maldacena and Ooguri in "Strings in AdS₃ and the SL(2,R) WZW Model. Part 1: The Spectrum" (hep-th/0001053, 2000), which proposed and justified a Hilbert space containing both continuous-series and discrete-series representations (with the bound 1/2 < j < (k-1)/2 for discrete series) together with all spectrally-flowed images, thereby accommodating the long strings and resolving the j < k/2 puzzle. Part 2 (hep-th/0005183) showed modular invariance via the Euclidean black hole one-loop partition function, and Part 3 (hep-th/0111180) computed correlation functions. The classical and path-integral aspects, target-space boundary conditions, and role of continuous series are addressed in this body of work and subsequent literature.

status_evidence.title: Strings in AdS_3 and the SL(2,R) WZW Model. Part 1: The Spectrum
status_evidence.snippet: Proposes spectrum including discrete and continuous representations of SL(2,R) and spectral flow, providing semi-classical match and full quantum analysis of strings on AdS3.
status_evidence.claim: Resolves the j<k/2 bound and clarifies the role of continuous series in the AdS3 string spectrum.

status_evidence.title: Strings in AdS_3 and the SL(2,R) WZW Model. Part 2: Euclidean Black Hole
status_evidence.snippet: One-loop partition function on Euclidean BTZ; modular invariant and consistent with Part 1 spectrum.
status_evidence.claim: Confirms the proposed spectrum via modular invariance.

status_evidence.title: Strings in AdS_3 and the SL(2,R) WZW Model. Part 3: Correlation Functions
status_evidence.snippet: Computes correlation functions in the SL(2,R) WZW model relevant to strings on AdS3.
status_evidence.claim: Completes the dynamical analysis of the model.
